issue.title: tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py still forks epic-plan-launch lock holders from multi-threaded xdist workers
issue.description:
ROOT CAUSE (already proven on a sibling node): forking from a multi-threaded process inherits only the calling thread, so any lock or buffer another thread held at fork time is inherited in an indeterminate state. Under xdist, every worker carries a live execnet receiver thread, so every multiprocessing.get_context('fork') in a test is a fork-after-threads hazard. Epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.5 proved this is not theoretical: it was the root cause of tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py::test_headless_epic_approval_submits_while_inflight_launch_holds_anchor (task sase-nz), which accumulated 12 full-run failure records across six workspaces and twelve HEADs between 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-17 before b6246f1cf fixed it.

WHAT IS LEFT: tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py carries the identical pattern. Two module-level helpers, _acquire_epic_plan_launch_lock (line 53) and _hold_epic_plan_launch_lock (line 62), are each launched through multiprocessing.get_context('fork') at four call sites (lines 322, 346, 420, 492), guarded by the same wall-clock bounds the fixed node used: acquired.wait(2.0), process.join(timeout=2.0), and release.wait(5.0) inside the holder.

EVIDENCE THAT THE PATTERN IS STILL LIVE: after b6246f1cf, an xdist parallel run (-n 2 --dist=loadfile) of tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py plus tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py emitted the multi-threaded-fork DeprecationWarning naming ONLY the four test_sdd_git_contention.py nodes, and zero from the fixed file. None of these four nodes is a reported flake today, so this is preventive work on a proven-hazardous pattern, not a live red.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DIRECTLY REUSABLE: b6246f1cf added _foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder to tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py, an in-process @contextmanager that opens the real lock path via the production _epic_plan_launch_lock_path(anchor), takes fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB), writes the same holder JSON the production epic_plan_launch_lock writes (pid/op/plan_file/started_at), and self-checks that a second open() of the path is refused with BlockingIOError before yielding. This works because flock ownership belongs to the open file description rather than the process, so an in-process holder is indistinguishable from a foreign one to the code under test. Port that seam to these four call sites (a shared test helper is the natural home, since two files now want it) and drop the wall-clock waits, which become unnecessary once the contended window is bounded by a with-block instead of a timer.

SCOPE: tests only; no production code should change. Verify with a full parallel lane run and confirm the multi-threaded-fork DeprecationWarning no longer names any node in this file.

PROPOSED BY: phase bead sase-ns.6.6.5 of epic sase-ns.6.6, as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on 2026-08-17T08:52:25Z; routed to a task bead by that epic's land agent, which independently re-verified the four fork call sites in the current tree.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-nz — the sibling node this pattern already broke (test_headless_epic_approval_submits_while_inflight_launch_holds_anchor). Closed as done by epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.5; its fix commit b6246f1cf contains the _foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder seam this task should reuse.

RELATED: sase-j7 — in-progress epic owning process-global state leaking between tests. Adjacent but not the same mechanism: this is fork-after-threads inheritance, not a leaked module global. That epic's leak detector (tests/_global_state_leak_detector.py) does not currently instrument interpreter thread count at fork time, which is recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on sase-j7 itself.

FIXED. tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py no longer forks: 'grep -n "fork|multiprocessing"' now matches only two docstring lines describing what was replaced, and the 'import multiprocessing' is gone.

WHAT LANDED: a _ForeignEpicLaunchLockWorker helper replacing multiprocessing.get_context('fork') at all four call sites (the former lines 322, 346, 420, 492). It runs the target in a daemon thread inside a fresh contextvars.Context. Two independent facts make that a faithful foreign holder: flock ownership belongs to the open file description rather than the process, so a second open() of the lock path from this same process is refused exactly as from a separate process; and the production re-entrancy guard _held_epic_plan_launch_anchors is a ContextVar, so a fresh Context gives the thread the empty set a separate process would start with, preventing a short-circuit past the real flock wait.

DIVERGENCE FROM THIS BEAD'S PRESCRIPTION, DELIBERATE: this bead asked to port _foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder from b6246f1cf and drop the wall-clock waits. I did not, for two reasons. (1) That seam is a contextmanager -- it can hold the lock, but it cannot block-then-acquire. Site 1 (test_epic_plan_launch_lock_blocks_other_process_for_same_canonical_anchor) asserts a foreign party is refused while we hold and succeeds after we release, which inherently needs a concurrent actor, so a with-block cannot bound it. (2) The thread runs the real production epic_plan_launch_lock, so the holder-identity JSON asserted by the expiry test (op, plan_file, started_at) is produced by production code instead of hand-rolled in the test, which is strictly more faithful than the contextmanager's manual json.dump. The waits that remain are therefore load-bearing, not leftover timers. The shared-helper consolidation the bead suggested is not done; tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py keeps its own seam.

ASSERTION CHANGE: 'holder pid {process.pid}' became 'holder pid {os.getpid()}'. Inherent to any in-process seam, including the one this bead prescribed, since the holder JSON records the current pid either way.

VERIFICATION: 19 passed serially in the file; the blocking site measures 0.16s call time, confirming it genuinely waited on the real flock rather than short-circuiting. 41 passed across tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py + tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py run with -W error::DeprecationWarning, so no multi-threaded-fork DeprecationWarning fires -- a stronger check than this bead's 'confirm the warning names no node in this file', since a fork warning requires a fork call site and none remain. The bead's -n 2 --dist=loadfile lane could not run: the SASE pytest worker-token broker was fully subscribed by other agents (one 'scoped' holder had held 14 tokens for ~2.8h), so the xdist form was starved; the static + escalated-warning evidence above covers the same property. Scoped lane: 485 passed. Whole-repo lint gates green except a pre-existing _lint-symvision failure from closed bead sase-op.3, unrelated to this diff and routed to active epic sase-op.

SCOPE HELD: tests only; no production code changed.
